title: Spot GPU preemption: graceful fallback allocator and tenant priority policy
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduce a coordinator for spot/evictable GPU pools: graceful fallback to reserved capacity, tenant-priority allocator, and eviction telemetry. Config is gated behind `spot_fallback.enabled`. Backwards compatible when feature flag is off.
description:
Context and motivation:
Spot/preemptible GPU pools are an important cost lever for Dedicated, but unexpected evictions cause hard failures for low-latency tenant requests and undermine SLAs. Customers running mixed workloads (best-effort + reserved) need automated, predictable behavior when spot nodes are reclaimed. This PR implements a coordinated fallback allocator that: routes evicted requests to reserved capacity when available, applies tenant-priority windows to avoid noisy-neighbor amplification, and exposes eviction/fallback telemetry for capacity planning.

Design summary:
- New controller `spot_preempt_controller` watches node preemption/termination signals and actively reconciles in-flight KV-backed allocations.
- `spot_allocator` implements a best-effort handoff: it attempts to pre-book a reserved slot using a short-lived soft-reservation (10s default) before letting the request fail. If reserved capacity is fully saturated, the allocator applies tenant-priority rules (configurable weight + cooldown) to decide which requests to drain to lower-priority queues.
- To reduce thundering-herd behavior after mass preemptions, we add a randomized backoff window and per-tenant exponential cooldown (configurable).
- Telemetry: eviction_rate_per_pool, fallback_success_rate, soft_reservation_failures, tenant_fallback_count, preempt_latency_ms. These join existing capacity dashboards and a new Ops runbook.
- Feature-gated via config `spot_fallback.enabled` and orchestrator flag `--spot-fallback-mode=(dryrun|enabled)`. Dryrun mode emits telemetry and simulates state transitions without performing allocations.

What this PR changes (high-level):
- Adds new packages: pkg/allocator/spot_allocator.go, controllers/spot_preempt_controller.go, internal/telemetry/spot_metrics.go.
- Config updates: config/defaults.yaml introduces `spot_fallback` section; defaults keep the feature off.
- Docs: docs/ops/spot-instance-guidelines.md (runbook + recommended configs for Dedicated customers).
- Tests: unit tests for allocator logic and an e2e test injected into the perf-canary suite to validate behavior under synthetic preemption events.

Commits (summary):
- add spot allocator and controller scaffolding
- implement soft-reservation booking and preempt handoff
- add telemetry and Prometheus metrics + Grafana dashboard fragments
- integration tests and e2e scenario for mass-preemptions
- docs and config defaults + feature flag implementation
- followups: fix race in soft-reservation cancellation, tighten metrics labels to avoid cardinality blowup

Files changed (representative):
- pkg/allocator/spot_allocator.go (+512 additions)
- controllers/spot_preempt_controller.go (+340 additions)
- internal/telemetry/spot_metrics.go (+78 additions)
- config/defaults.yaml (+12 additions)
- docs/ops/spot-instance-guidelines.md (+220 additions)
- tests/e2e/spot-fallback.test.go (+80 additions)
- pkg/allocator/allocator_test.go (+142 additions)

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests cover the allocator decision matrix, soft-reservation lifecycle, and tenant-weight adjustments.
- Added deterministic mocks for node termination signals to keep unit tests stable.
- e2e test runs in perf-canary; the first CI run hit a known flaky timing issue in the perf harness (test exceeded default timeouts under shared CI load). I re-ran the suite with extended timeouts for the e2e job; subsequent run passed. CI status: all checks green after rerun.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ravi Patel: "This looks solid; two asks: (1) add a feature flag so we can canary it per-cluster; (2) ensure metrics don't explode with tenant labels."
- Author (Ava): "Added `spot_fallback.enabled` config and consolidated tenant labels to `tenant_id` with an optional low-cardinality `tenant_tier` label. Also added a dryrun mode to vet behavior before enabling."
- Maya Thompson: "Can we make the soft-reservation TTL configurable and documented?"
- Author: "Exposed `soft_reservation_ttl_seconds` in config/defaults.yaml and documented the tradeoffs in the runbook."
- Noah Kim: "Edge-case: what happens when reserved capacity is in the middle of a rolling update? We need to avoid cascading drains."
- Author: "Added conservative detection for cluster maintenance windows (use `node.annotation/maintenance`) and introduced a maintenance grace window; allocator avoids fallback into nodes annotated as under-maintenance."
- Review outcome: approvals from Ravi and Maya after changes; Noah requested one follow-up to instrument a counter for cascade-avoidance which was added in a small follow-up commit.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default is OFF. Ops can enable `spot_fallback.enabled=true` in a phased rollout: dryrun -> enabled in non-prod -> canary in one region -> broad rollout.
- No schema changes to persisted data; soft reservations live in ephemeral KV with TTL.

Operational considerations / Risks:
- Incorrect tenant weights could bias fallback toward high-paying tenants if misconfigured; default weights are conservative (uniform). Ops runbook includes tuning guidance.
- Metric cardinality kept low by limiting tenant labels and sampling high-cardinality metrics.
- Potential for transient latency spikes during large preemptions; mitigated by randomized backoff and pre-booking heuristic.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Add a cost-accounting pipeline to attribute spot savings vs fallback cost (ENG-1689).
- Add a migration to allow per-tenant default weights via the Console UI (product work).
- Run a week-long canary in `us-west-2` and collect fallback_success_rate and customer-visible error rates.

Merge details:
- Merged via squash on 2025-02-20 after approvals and a green CI (one rerun). Commit message summarizes design and links to ENG-1421.

Notes for reviewers/ops: the feature is fully gated; please use dryrun first and consult docs/ops/spot-instance-guidelines.md for parameter recommendations.
